name: Fury

date.source: The fed’s own results address, eventarchives/Fury/09082002.html, read American-style. The document itself carries no date. Both components are twelve or under, so the reading is not proof against the day-month clash this project has found elsewhere; its sibling address names its own month in words (jun202003).

notes: All eight matches on the card are structured. A Mumrat/Coley Walsh backstage confrontation between matches 4 and 5 is angle content and neither man is minted from it.

matches.note: Both men are thrown through a police-station window at different points. Notorious finishes with the Gangta's Paradise through the hood of a car.

matches.stipulation: Career Ending Match — the loser must leave UCWF
matches.note: Sex Drop, pin. Diablo is fired on the spot per the stipulation — and billed again regardless at Immortality 2002.
Mr. Wacko (c) retains with the Wacko Bomb.
The Krazy Kid wins the title with the Krazy Cutter.
The G's win by disqualification: Homefry passes Playa 69 a steel chair mid-match and the referee calls for the bell.
Blaze (billed bare, c) is driven to the thumbtacks by the Easton Bomb for the pin.

Scorpion (c) retains, finishing with Scorpion's Poison. Big Poppa Pimp enters with valets billed Skinny Sharon and Slim Susie, neither minted. Post-match, Johnny Johnson attacks Scorpion with a kendo stick and takes the belt, cutting a promo naming an August 17 national-debut target — an angle beat, not part of the match, and a date that predates this show's own.
Bobby Linken (c) retains with the Terminator.

appearances.note: Cuts a ring promo aimed at Coley Walsh, calling out his stable; Walsh runs in and the two brawl until security separates them.
Runs in on Mumrat's own ring promo and brawls with him until security breaks it up.

name: Immortality 2002

date.source: The fed’s own event-archive address, eventarchives/PPV/Immortality2002.html; the document itself carries no date.

matches.note: Bossa Nova wins with the Bossa Blast.
Soul Destroyer, pin.
Mike Gayed wins with the Supper DDT. The G's (Homefry & Playa 69) run in immediately after and beat down all three losers — an angle beat, not part of the match.
The Krazy-Wacko Connection win the titles back with a shooting star press.
Mr. Wacko wins the title with a backslide, taking it from The Fox (c).

Ace Of Spades (c) grounds Jinx with The Crossover and pins him with a German Suplex bridge, but his own shoulders are down at the same moment; referee Gangsta Mac counts three on both men and the announce team declares the finish unresolved (“WHO THE HELL WON! ... I guess we will have to wait and find out!!!”). No title change is recorded on this evidence; Ace Of Spades is not shown losing the Universal title again until CM2 is billed champion at the next surviving show.
Crash Paradise enters as champion, accompanied by valet Makayla Royal (not minted), who physically interferes. Scorpion wins the title, finishing with a cross torn off a church wall.

matches.stipulation: UCWF Extreme Championship — 1st fall of a Hell in a Cell (2nd fall below is for the World title)
matches.note: Blaze (billed bare, c) retains, forcing Brax to tap to the camel clutch.

matches.stipulation: UCWF World Championship — 2nd fall of the same Hell in a Cell
matches.note: A chaotic extended brawl inside the cage — Scorpion and James Hunter Cameron (not minted) attack Bobby Linken; Mumrat and Jinx (neither minted) defend him; a masked man teams with a returning Fox against Scorpion, then unmasks as a debuting Solidus (not minted), revealing a new stable, “Unforeseen Vengence,” with Brax, Fox and a returning Coley Walsh (none minted from this angle alone). Bobby Linken (c) retains, pinning Brax through a hole in the cage roof.

appearances.note: Runs in with Scorpion during the World title cage brawl to double-team Bobby Linken; driven off by Mumrat and Jinx.
Accompanies Crash Paradise to the ring carrying weapons and physically interferes in his Intercontinental title match against Scorpion.
Accompanies Bobby Linken to the ring, fights off James Hunter Cameron and Scorpion during the World title cage brawl, and is speared and slammed through the cage roof by a returning Coley Walsh.

Returns mid-match during the Extreme/World Hell in a Cell, spears Mumrat and slams him through the cage roof, then joins Brax, The Fox and a newly unmasked Solidus in revealing the stable Unforeseen Vengeance.

A masked man who teams with a returning Fox against Scorpion, then unmasks post-match as Solidus, Brax's own trainee, and joins him, The Fox and a returning Coley Walsh in forming the stable Unforeseen Vengeance.

notes: All eight of the card's own matches are structured. Match 6 (Jinx vs Ace Of Spades for the UCWF Universal Championship) resolves as a declared double-pin — the show's own text has referee Gangsta Mac count three on both men's shoulders and the announce team refuse to name a winner (“WHO THE HELL WON! ... I guess we will have to wait and find out!!!”) — recorded with result: "double-pin" rather than a guessed winner, per the schema's own declared-outcome doctrine.

name: Resurrection

date.source: The fed’s own event-archive address, eventarchives/PPV/Resurrection2003.html; the document itself carries no date.

notes: All six matches on the card are structured.

matches.note: The Fox wins the title from The Krazy Kid (c) with “Outfoxing The Fox.”
“QBz Finest” Blaze wins the title from Mr. Wacko (c) with the Special Delivery.
The Krazy-Wacko Connection (c) retain with the Krazy Cutter.

Rich Bitch wins the title from A.J. Simmons (c) with the Bank Rupt. Mid-match action repeatedly names a third figure, “Preston T Wallace II,” despite only two men being introduced — read as a leftover simulator/sim-name artifact rather than a third wrestler, and not minted on this evidence alone.

matches.stipulation: Winner gets a UCWF World title shot at that year's Fury
matches.note: Supper DDT into a backslide, pin.

matches.stipulation: UCWF World Championship — special guest referee: UCWF owner Mumrat
matches.note: The Notorious Don Joe Giovanni wins the title with the Wise Guy, counted by Mumrat himself. Johnny Johnson protests a quick count afterward; a debuting Sean Johnson silently teases from the entrance — an angle beat, not part of the match.

appearances.note: Special guest referee for the World Championship main event; counts the pin himself and hands the belt to The Notorious Don Joe Giovanni.

name: Wrestle Insanity

date.source: The fed’s own event-archive address, eventarchives/PPV/WrestleInsanity2003.html; the document itself carries no date.

notes: All six of the card's own matches are structured, including the Tag Team Championship match (order 3) naming A.C.E.'s own Ace Of Spades and Crash Paradise.

matches.note: The Krazy Kid (c) retains with the Krazy Cutter.
Mr. Wacko (c) retains with a backslide.
A.C.E. (Ace Of Spades and Crash Paradise) win the titles from the Krazy-Wacko Connection (c), Ace Of Spades pinning The Krazy Kid with The Crossover.

matches.stipulation: UCWF Extreme Championship — Flaming Hell in a Cell
matches.note: Both men's shoulders are down together; the referee declares a draw. Flashing Thunder (c) retains.

“QBz Finest” Blaze wins the title from Notorious (c) with the Special Delivery. Notorious attacks Blaze and the referee with a chair afterward and is suspended by Mumrat — an angle beat, not part of the match.
Johnny Johnson (c) is distracted by a fictional in-arena news report naming him alongside a “convicted murderer,” and Bobby Linken rolls him up for the pin and the title.

appearances.note: Suspends Notorious for a post-match chair assault on Blaze and the referee, effective through that week.

name: Breakout

date.source: The fed’s own event-archive address, eventarchives/PPV/Breakout2003.html; the document itself carries no date beyond its own title.

matches.stipulation: Winner gets a UCWF Universal Championship shot
matches.note: Universal Champion Blaze runs in mid-match and lays out both men; the referee calls for the bell with no winner declared.
“Prime Time” The Vine (c) retains with the Vine Bomb.

matches.stipulation: UCWF Universal Championship — Six Pack Challenge
matches.note: “QBz Finest” Blaze enters as champion. The Fox wins the title, pinning Jason Compton with a German suplex bridge. A referee billed only “Bobby” works the match — a different figure from competitor Bobby Linken, a same-first-name mix-up in the source text, not minted.

matches.stipulation: UCWF Extreme Championship — Barbwire Beat Down Match
matches.note: The match header names Osbourne's second opponent “The Fox Johnson,” but the body text only ever fights “the 'Just Too Damn Strong' Sean Johnson” — a document-internal naming inconsistency, not a fourth wrestler. Flashing Thunder is eliminated mid-match (thrown off the stage through a barbwire table); Osbourne (c) and Sean Johnson both collapse from blood loss and the bout is declared a draw, so Osbourne retains.

matches.stipulation: UCWF Intercontinental Championship — tournament final, billed “Best Friends Battle”
matches.note: Mr. Wacko is ring-announced the new Intercontinental Champion.

matches.stipulation: UCWF World Championship — Breakout match (a dome-type cage over the ring, escaped only through a roof hatch reached by a 20-foot ladder), billed “Part 1: A Battle For Respect II”
matches.note: Ace Of Spades wins the title, kicking The Notorious Don Joe Giovanni off the ladder before pulling himself out through the roof hatch.

notes: All six of the card's own matches are structured, including the World Championship main event (order 6), a Breakout dome-cage match billed “Part 1: A Battle For Respect II.” The Notorious Don Joe Giovanni (c) loses the title per the show's own text (“Your Winner and NEW World Champion, Ace Of Spades!”).

name: Fury

date.source: The results page’s own heading: “UCWF Fury Results - 6/20/03 / Live from Green Bay, Wisconsin”.

notes: Six of the card's own matches are structured, including the World Championship main event (order 6), a 60-minute Hell In A Cell Ironman match refereed by The KO Kid. The Notorious Don Joe Giovanni retains per the show's own text, time expiring with Ace Of Spades collapsed from blood loss; both he and referee The KO Kid are credited here with kind:"angle" for their own appearances. Wes Easton hosts a pre-match talk-show segment (“The End of the Road”) previewing the main event; not a match of his own.

matches.note: “Prime Time” The Vine wins the title from The Fox (c) with the Vine Bomb.

matches.stipulation: UCWF Extreme Championship — Deathmatch, billed Osbourne's UCWF debut
matches.note: Bryon Wade Osbourne wins the title with a front-face slam finisher (called both “Tazmission” and “Forty OZ. Casualty” in the text).

matches.stipulation: UCWF International Championship tournament — first round
matches.note: Mr. Wacko advances with the Wacko Bomb.

matches.stipulation: UCWF International Championship tournament — first round
matches.note: The Krazy Kid advances with the Krazy Cutter. (Spelled “Santa Clause” in this document's own body text, “Santa Claus” in its header — the same inconsistency the Breakout script also carries.)

matches.stipulation: Loser Leaves UCWF — no title on the line
matches.note: Texas Cloverleaf, tapout. Johnny Johnson is written out of the fed per the stipulation.

matches.stipulation: UCWF World Championship — 60-minute Hell In A Cell Ironman match, special guest referee The KO Kid
matches.note: The Notorious Don Joe Giovanni (c) retains, three falls to two, time expiring with Ace Of Spades collapsed from blood loss as Giovanni lines up a barbwire bat swing he never throws.

appearances.note: As “President Mumrat,” adds a street fight stipulation to the Mr. Wacko/Jason Compton/Bobby Linken International Championship tournament match.
